t: In front of you is the Tower of London, a castle on the north bank of the Thames, built as two rings of defensive walls around a moat. William the Conqueror founded it at the end of 1066, and his White Tower, built in 1078, gives the castle its name. It was first resented as a symbol of oppression. It was also a royal residence. Over the centuries it became a place of death for the great. Anne Boleyn and Lady Jane Grey died here. So did Henry the Sixth. Young Edward the Fifth, never crowned, died here in 1483.
